To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) there is a sharp decline in the public's confidence in American institutions and leaders; (b) the public's trust in government has declined more sharply than its trust in other institutions; (c) there is a significant correlation between confidence in institutions and confidence in the government; (d) the public's confidence declined most in the 1960s, but it has continued to decline in the 1970s; (e) there is a strong relationship between confidence and political participation;

the decline of confidence in American institutions began in the late 1960s and has continued through the 1970s; the decline is most pronounced in confidence in government and the presidency and in confidence in business and the economy; confidence is highest in the military; and the decline of confidence is not confined to the United States but is also found in other Western democracies.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following: (a) the decline in public confidence in the major institutions of society, (b) the decline in the public's confidence in the political leadership of those institutions, and (c) the public's perception of the reasons for this decline in confidence.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
public confidence in American institutions is at a low ebb.
the decline in confidence in American political institutions is real and widespread.
the American public's trust in the institutions of American society and government has declined since the mid-196os.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the decline in confidence has been most pronounced in the political sphere and that, with the exception of the presidency, it has not been confined to any particular party or ideology, nor is it confined to any particular region of the country.
the public's confidence in American institutions has been declining for at least two decades.
the decline has been broad-based, encompassing most major social institutions and political leaders, and has been most severe for the presidency, for Congress, and for the press.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the decline in confidence is real, is widespread, and appears to be continuing.
there has been a decline in confidence in the American government and its institutions.
the decline in trust in American institutions is real, and that it is not confined to any particular segment of the American public.
